coverage: Reviewed embedded components and pinned dependencies; source paths are scope hints. Not exhaustive runtime dependency or file-level clearance.

components.name: librtlsdr desktop release builds

components.name: libairspy

components.name: IBM Plex fonts
components.assessment: Compiled into Qt resource bundle; all Qt builds must retain the notice. Official Qt artifact is Android.

components.name: Recorded regression fixtures
components.assessment: Includes unknown-permission recordings and specifically attributed assets; assess each asset. Source-only, not binary payload.

components.name: gqrx-scanner rig control portions
components.assessment: Retained neural75 MIT grant from initial commit 88c8999d5559211dc655d580940b0e917488c334; LICENSE history is unchanged since 2017.

components.name: SoapySDR
components.assessment: Pinned 0.8.1 library, built from the same commit for the AppImage (libSoapySDR, without SoapySDR's programs) and the Windows ZIP (SoapySDR.dll). The BSL-1.0 text names no holder; SoapySDR-COPYRIGHT.txt lists every holder the compiled library and SoapySDRUtil sources name (Josh Blum, Bastille Networks, Coburn Wightman, Nicholas Corgan) and SoapySDRUtil's public-domain MSVC getopt.h from mingw-w64. The macOS DMG bundles Homebrew's build, which this record does not cover.

components.name: SoapySDRUtil
components.assessment: SoapySDR's device tool, SoapySDRUtil.exe in bin\ of the Windows ZIP, built by the soapysdr overlay's tools feature from the commit SoapySDR.dll comes from; its MSVC getopt.h is mingw-w64's public-domain file. SoapySDR-COPYRIGHT.txt lists the holders its sources name. The AppImage builds SoapySDR without its programs.

components.name: SoapyAirspy module
components.assessment: Pinned 0.2.1 SoapySDR module (airspySupport.dll) in the Windows ZIP, built against the airspy overlay; its upstream LICENSE.txt ships as licenses/SoapyAirspy-MIT.txt.

components.name: SoapyHackRF module
components.assessment: Pinned 0.3.6 SoapySDR module (HackRFSupport.dll) in the Windows ZIP. The upstream LICENSE names no holder, so the shipped notice (licenses/SoapyHackRF-MIT.txt) adds the source headers' holders.

components.name: libhackrf
components.assessment: Pinned v2026.01.3 library (hackrf.dll) in the Windows ZIP, built from host/libhackrf/src only; the repository's GPL-2.0 firmware and tools are not built. The shipped notice (licenses/libhackrf-BSD-3-Clause.txt) carries every source-header holder and the HackRF trademark notice.

components.name: libusb Windows build
components.assessment: libusb-1.0.dll in the Windows ZIP, which librtlsdr, libairspy and libhackrf load; vcpkg's libusb port at the manifest baseline (1.0.30, no project pin). Its COPYING is the retained one and ships as licenses/libusb-LGPL-2.1-or-later.txt; libusb-COPYRIGHT.txt, shipped as licenses/libusb-COPYRIGHT.txt, carries the holders and attributions of every source the Windows DLL is built from and the upstream AUTHORS file. Corresponding source remains open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: PThreads4W
components.assessment: pthreadVC3.dll in the Windows ZIP, which librtlsdr, libairspy and libhackrf load; vcpkg's pthreads port at the manifest baseline (PThreads4W 3.0.0, no project pin). Its LICENSE, NOTICE and the CONTRIBUTORS file the NOTICE refers to, from that release's archive, ship as licenses/PThreads4W-Apache-2.0.txt, licenses/PThreads4W-NOTICE.txt and licenses/PThreads4W-CONTRIBUTORS.txt.

components.name: codec2
components.license_declared: LGPL-2.1-only AND LGPL-2.1-or-later AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause
components.license_concluded: LGPL-2.1-only AND LGPL-2.1-or-later AND BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause
components.assessment: The codec2 library from the pinned arancormonk/codec2 commit (CODEC2_SHA; release 1.2.0, a fork of drowe67/codec2), which dsd-neo uses for M17 voice: codec2.dll in the Windows ZIP, built by the codec2 overlay; the same overlay's static library, linked into the Android app (arm64-android-static); and the shared library the Linux AppImage builds from the same commit and bundles. Each build compiles the sources of src/CMakeLists.txt's CODEC2_SRCS with LPCNet off. Most files grant the LGPL 2.1 without "or later"; the Valenti code in src/mpdecode_core.c is LGPL-2.1-or-later, src/kiss_fft.c and src/kiss_fftr.c are BSD-3-Clause (Mark Borgerding) and src/lpcnet_freq.c is BSD-2-Clause (Mozilla). src/varicode.c, varicode.h and varicode_table.h grant "the GNU General Public License version 2.1", a version the FSF never published; they are recorded as LGPL-2.1-only, the license of codec2's COPYING and README.md. LICENSES/codec2-LGPL-2.1.txt is the upstream COPYING, unmodified. LICENSES/codec2-NOTICES.txt names the holders of the compiled sources and reproduces the BSD and Valenti notices from the pinned archive (its SHA512 is CODEC2_TARBALL_SHA512). LICENSES/LicenseRef-codec2-varicode.txt reproduces the varicode grant unmodified, with a note stating that reading; it records the reading, not a separate license, so no LicenseRef enters the license expression. The Windows ZIP, the APK and the AppImage carry the three as licenses/codec2-LGPL-2.1.txt, licenses/codec2-NOTICES.txt and licenses/LicenseRef-codec2-varicode.txt, and the ZIP also carries the copyright file the overlay installs (share/codec2/copyright, the same COPYING) as licenses/codec2-copyright.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: PortAudio
components.assessment: portaudio.dll in the Windows ZIP, dsd-neo.exe's audio input and output, built by the portaudio overlay (vcpkg's port at port-version 8) from release v19.7.0 (PORTAUDIO_SHA) with MSVC: the common and Windows sources and the DirectSound, MME, WASAPI and WDM-KS host APIs. The overlay passes PA_USE_ASIO=OFF, so the Steinberg ASIO SDK, which has its own license, is never compiled in. Every compiled file is under the PortAudio license, which is the MIT license; the non-binding requests after it are outside the license by its own words. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/portaudio/copyright, the upstream LICENSE.txt, which names Ross Bencina and Phil Burk) as licenses/portaudio-copyright.txt, and packaging/windows/portaudio-NOTICES.txt, the holder lines of every compiled file and header (also Andrew Baldwin, Robert Marsanyi, David Viens and Dmitry Kostjuchenko) from the pinned archive, as licenses/portaudio-NOTICES.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: PDCurses
components.assessment: pdcurses.dll in the Windows ZIP, dsd-neo.exe's terminal interface; vcpkg's pdcurses port at the manifest baseline (PDCurses 3.9, wmcbrine/PDCurses tag 3.9), built from pdcurses/, wincon/ and common/ (wincon/Makefile.vc). Upstream releases the files of those directories to the public domain; the x11/ files with their own license are not built. SPDX has no identifier for a public-domain dedication, hence the LicenseRef. LICENSES/LicenseRef-PDCurses-Public-Domain.txt reproduces upstream's statements from the pinned archive and ships as licenses/LicenseRef-PDCurses-Public-Domain.txt. The copyright file the port installs is vcpkg's own paraphrase of them, not upstream text, so the ZIP no longer carries it. A public-domain dedication may not take effect everywhere, and upstream gives no fallback license. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: OpenSSL libcrypto
components.assessment: libcrypto-3-x64.dll in the Windows ZIP; vcpkg's openssl port at the manifest baseline (3.6.5, tag openssl-3.6.5), configured VC-WIN64A, shared, with static engines. dsd-neo links only libcrypto and libcurl uses Windows' Schannel, so the ZIP carries no libssl and no legacy provider module. The library is under the Apache License 2.0; crypto/siphash/siphash.c is dedicated under CC0-1.0, and the SEED sources (crypto/seed/, include/openssl/seed.h) also carry the Korea Information Security Agency's terms, whose conditions cover source redistribution (LicenseRef-OpenSSL-KISA-SEED). Files also offered under other terms (crypto/LPdir_win*.c, crypto/x509/v3_pci*.c, the Camellia and CRYPTOGAMS assembly) are used under the Apache License 2.0. OpenSSL ships no NOTICE file. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/openssl/copyright, LICENSE.txt) as licenses/openssl-copyright.txt; packaging/windows/OpenSSL-AUTHORS.md, the upstream AUTHORS.md unmodified, as licenses/OpenSSL-AUTHORS.md; packaging/windows/OpenSSL-NOTICES.txt, the other holders named in the compiled sources with their dual-license, CC0 and public-domain notes, as licenses/OpenSSL-NOTICES.txt; and LICENSES/LicenseRef-OpenSSL-KISA-SEED.txt, KISA's notice from crypto/seed/seed.c, as licenses/LicenseRef-OpenSSL-KISA-SEED.txt; each from the pinned archive. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: libcurl
components.assessment: libcurl.dll in the Windows ZIP; vcpkg's curl port at the manifest baseline (8.23.0, tag curl-8_23_0) with its default ssl feature, which on Windows is Schannel: libcurl loads zlib's z.dll and Windows DLLs only, no OpenSSL. The compiled sources are under the curl license, except lib/curlx/inet_ntop.c and inet_pton.c (ISC). The port's vcpkg.json also declares BSD-3-Clause; no file in the pinned archive carries it, and its one BSD-licensed file, tests/server/tftpd.c, is not part of libcurl. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/curl/copyright: COPYING and the inet_ntop.c notice) as licenses/curl-copyright.txt, and packaging/windows/curl-NOTICES.txt, the holder lines of the compiled sources that name holders other than Daniel Stenberg, from the pinned archive, as licenses/curl-NOTICES.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: Expat
components.assessment: libexpat.dll in the Windows ZIP; vcpkg's expat port at the manifest baseline (2.9.0, tag R_2_9_0): expat/lib/xcs.c, xmlparse.c, xmlrole.c, xmltok.c and random_rand_s.c. MIT, with lib/siphash.h under CC0-1.0. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/expat/copyright: expat/COPYING and siphash.h) as licenses/expat-copyright.txt, and packaging/windows/expat-NOTICES.txt, the holder lines of every compiled file and header from the pinned archive, as licenses/expat-NOTICES.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: zlib
components.assessment: z.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libcurl loads; vcpkg's zlib port at the manifest baseline (1.3.2, tag v1.3.2), the library sources only (nothing from contrib/ is built). The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/zlib/copyright, the upstream LICENSE) as licenses/zlib-copyright.txt; it is the whole zlib license and names both holders, Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: libsndfile
components.license_declared: LGPL-2.1-or-later AND LGPL-2.0-or-later AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND TU-Berlin-1.0 AND LicenseRef-Sun-G72x
components.license_concluded: LGPL-2.1-or-later AND LGPL-2.0-or-later AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND TU-Berlin-1.0 AND LicenseRef-Sun-G72x
components.assessment: sndfile.dll in the Windows ZIP, dsd-neo.exe's audio file reader and writer; vcpkg's libsndfile port at the manifest baseline (1.2.2, libsndfile/libsndfile tag 1.2.2) with its default external-libs and mpeg features. The DLL compiles libsndfile's own sources (LGPL-2.1-or-later; src/ima_oki_adpcm.c and .h LGPL-2.0-or-later) and three bundled codecs: GSM 06.10 (src/GSM610, the Technische Universitaet Berlin notice, TU-Berlin-1.0), G.72x (src/G72x, Sun Microsystems' unrestricted-use notice, LicenseRef-Sun-G72x) and ALAC (src/ALAC, Apple, Apache-2.0; the archive has no NOTICE file for it). src/ogg.c, ogg_opus.c and ogg_vorbis.c reproduce Xiph.Org BSD-3-Clause notices. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/libsndfile/copyright, the LGPL 2.1 COPYING) as licenses/libsndfile-copyright.txt; src/GSM610/COPYRIGHT and src/ALAC/LICENSE, unmodified, as licenses/libsndfile-GSM610-COPYRIGHT.txt and licenses/libsndfile-ALAC-Apache-2.0.txt; Sun's notice from src/G72x/g72x.c as licenses/LicenseRef-Sun-G72x.txt; and packaging/windows/libsndfile-NOTICES.txt, the holder lines of every compiled file and the Xiph notices, as licenses/libsndfile-NOTICES.txt; each from the pinned archive. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: libFLAC
components.assessment: FLAC.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile loads; vcpkg's libflac port at the manifest baseline (1.5.0, xiph/flac tag 1.5.0): libFLAC only, without assembly, under BSD-3-Clause; its MD5 code is public domain. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/libflac/copyright, the upstream COPYING.Xiph, which names both holders, Josh Coalson and the Xiph.Org Foundation) as licenses/libflac-copyright.txt. FLAC++.dll is built but nothing loads it, so the ZIP does not carry it. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: libogg
components.assessment: ogg.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile and its codecs load; vcpkg's libogg port at the manifest baseline (1.3.6, xiph/ogg tag v1.3.6): src/bitwise.c and src/framing.c, under BSD-3-Clause (Xiph.Org Foundation; framing.c's CRC code derives from Ross Williams' public-domain code). The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/libogg/copyright, the upstream COPYING, which names the Xiph.org Foundation) as licenses/libogg-copyright.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: libvorbis
components.assessment: vorbis.dll and vorbisenc.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile loads; vcpkg's libvorbis port at the manifest baseline (1.3.7, xiph/vorbis tag v1.3.7). vorbisfile.dll is built but nothing loads it, so the ZIP does not carry it. BSD-3-Clause (Xiph.Org Foundation); lib/lpc.c, in vorbis.dll, also preserves Jutta Degener and Carsten Bormann's Technische Universitaet Berlin notice and asks that it be kept unmodified (TU-Berlin-1.0). The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/libvorbis/copyright, the upstream COPYING) as licenses/libvorbis-copyright.txt, and packaging/windows/libvorbis-lpc-NOTICE.txt, lib/lpc.c lines 17-43 from the pinned archive, unmodified, as licenses/libvorbis-lpc-NOTICE.txt. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: Opus
components.assessment: opus.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile loads; vcpkg's opus port at the manifest baseline (1.6.1, xiph/opus tag v1.6.1), floating point for x64, with no deep-learning (DNN, DRED, OSCE) code. The compiled files carry the BSD-3-Clause license of Opus's COPYING or its two-clause form (BSD-2-Clause). The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/opus/copyright, COPYING) as licenses/opus-copyright.txt, and packaging/windows/opus-NOTICES.txt, the headers of the compiled files that name holders COPYING does not (Cisco Systems, Google, Arm Limited, Koen Vos, Vidyo, Parrot, John Ridges) and the two-clause text, from the pinned archive, as licenses/opus-NOTICES.txt. COPYING points to royalty-free patent licenses from Xiph.Org, Microsoft and Broadcom, which have conditions; they are not reviewed here. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: LAME
components.assessment: libmp3lame.DLL in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile loads; vcpkg's mp3lame port at the manifest baseline (LAME 3.100), built with MSVC from vc_solution/vc11_libmp3lame_dll.vcxproj: libmp3lame and, by its build files, the mpglib decoder. The file headers grant the GNU Library General Public License version 2 or any later version, and libmp3lame/gain_analysis.c and .h the GNU Lesser General Public License 2.1 or any later version. The port's vcpkg.json (LGPL-2.0-only) and the upstream README ("version 2"; "MPGLIB is released under the GPL") say otherwise; the file headers are followed. libmp3lame/fft.c names no license of its own and is taken as covered by the package's LGPL. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/mp3lame/copyright, the LGPL 2.0 COPYING) as licenses/mp3lame-copyright.txt; the LGPL 2.1 text (android/third_party/libusb/COPYING) as licenses/mp3lame-LGPL-2.1.txt; the upstream README and LICENSE, unmodified, as licenses/mp3lame-README.txt and licenses/mp3lame-LICENSE.txt; and packaging/windows/mp3lame-NOTICES.txt, the holder lines of the compiled files with mpglib/README and the header of libmp3lame/fft.c, as licenses/mp3lame-NOTICES.txt; each from the pinned archive. The README, mpglib/README and fft.c note possible patent claims; they are not reviewed here. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: mpg123
components.assessment: mpg123.dll in the Windows ZIP, which libsndfile loads; vcpkg's mpg123 port at the manifest baseline (1.33.7), libmpg123 only (libout123 and libsyn123 are built but nothing loads them, so the ZIP does not carry them). COPYING and every compiled file grant the LGPL 2.1 without "or later" (the port's vcpkg.json says LGPL-2.1-or-later); src/libmpg123/icy2utf8.c is under the MirOS license, which asks for its notice in an accompanying document, and src/libmpg123/layer3.c holds a short piece Mikko Tommila made freely usable. The ZIP carries the copyright file the port installs (share/mpg123/copyright, COPYING with the LGPL 2.1 and GPL 2 texts) as licenses/mpg123-copyright.txt; the upstream AUTHORS, unmodified, as licenses/mpg123-AUTHORS.txt; and packaging/windows/mpg123-NOTICES.txt, the icy2utf8.c and layer3.c notices, as licenses/mpg123-NOTICES.txt; each from the pinned archive. Corresponding source is open (CORRESPONDING-SOURCE).

components.name: Microsoft Visual C++ runtime
components.assessment: Microsoft's C and C++ runtime DLLs in bin\ of the Windows ZIP, as many of the files windows_release lists as its binaries import (the 2.12.1 ZIP carried MSVCP140.dll, VCRUNTIME140.dll and VCRUNTIME140_1.dll). tools/windows/stage_runtime_dlls.ps1 copies them unmodified from the x64 runtime folder of the toolset that built the release, VC\Redist\MSVC\<version>\x64\Microsoft.VC<toolset>.CRT, and never from System32; it and verify_release_tree.ps1 refuse any other Visual C++ runtime DLL and the debug runtime. Terms: the Distributable Code section of the Microsoft Software License Terms for Visual Studio (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/license-terms/) and its REDIST list, which lets a licensed Visual Studio user distribute the files of VC\Redist except its debug_nonredist folders: "Visual Studio Redistribution" for Visual Studio 2026 and later (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2026/redistribution) and "Visual Studio 2022 Redistribution" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/releases/2022/redistribution), retrieved 2026-11-18. The release relies on the maintainer's Visual Studio Community licence, the hosted runner being a Build Device hosted on Microsoft Azure; the licensing of the runner's preinstalled Visual Studio is not verified. The ZIP carries an end-user notice of the terms for these files (LicenseRef-Microsoft-Visual-CPP-Runtime.txt) and legal/msvc-runtime.md whenever it carries one of them, and the release job refuses a tree that carries one without both. legal/msvc-runtime.md quotes the terms, records how the release meets each condition (the protective terms, no Microsoft trademark in the program's name, the indemnity the Visual Studio 2026 terms require), and keeps the FSF GPL FAQ's contrary reading of GPLv3's System Libraries definition as a known, accepted risk.

components.name: vcpkg port recipes
components.assessment: The soapysdr and rtlsdr overlays are copies of vcpkg's builtin ports at the manifest baseline and the portaudio overlay of its port-version 8, each with dsd-neo changes its portfile names (GPL-3.0-or-later). vcpkg's LICENSE.txt at the baseline, with Microsoft's notice, is kept beside them as vcpkg-ports/LICENSE-vcpkg.txt. These are build recipes: no vcpkg code is compiled into a release package (the rtlsdr .diff files and jack.diff change build files; fix-guid-linker-errors.patch carries PortAudio's own upstream commits), so the packages do not carry the notice.
